intro: Step into Perge, an ancient city in Antalya province whose story reaches back to the 12th century BC. This was Pamphylia's grandest Roman city, famous for its colonnaded street and the water channel running down its centre.
history: Legend says Perge was founded by migrants after the Trojan War. In Roman times it was transformed into a monumental city, thanks to a benefactor named Plancia Magna.
structure-3: You are now in the Stadium, one of the best-preserved stadiums in Anatolia. Look at how the seating is carried: on seventy vaults, every third one an entrance and the rest shops. The north end closes in a horseshoe, while the south end is open. Imagine the crowds streaming in through those arches.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Hellenistic Gate, the Colonnaded Street, the Theatre and the Roman Baths.
facts: Did you know? A water channel ran down the centre of the 250-metre colonnaded street. It was the city's cooling system, ancient air-conditioning for the summer. Apollonius of Perga, who defined the conic sections, came from here: we owe him the words ellipse, parabola and hyperbola. And the city's greatest benefactor was a woman, Plancia Magna, who rebuilt its gate; her statues and inscriptions were found there.
outro: This brings our tour of Perge to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for walking with us, and enjoy your visit.
